Kuvitus: keittiön työtaso. Keskellä on m: Illustration: a kitchen worktop. In the middle is a black induction hob with a steel pan on the cooking zone, and steam rises from the pan. On the right a phone rests on a round wireless charger. On the wall at the left is a fibre router, with a thin optical cable running to it, and the end of the cable glows.
Periaatekuva langattomasta laturista siv: Schematic of a wireless charger in cross-section, field shape calculated: two panels. In each, at the bottom is the charging pad with the transmitter coil inside it, and above it is the phone, with a receiver coil of the same size in its base. The alternating current of the transmitter coil produces a magnetic field whose green field lines loop around the wires of the coil and pass upward through the middle of the coil; the green triangle at the centre of the coil shows the direction of the field. On the left the phone is 3 millimetres away, and six field lines pass through the receiver coil. On the right the phone is 20 millimetres away, and only one line passes through the receiver; the other lines turn back before reaching the phone. The lines passing through the receiver are drawn darker.
Periaatekuva induktioliedestä sivulta le: Schematic of an induction hob in cross-section, not to scale. At the top is a steel pan containing water. The pan stands on the glass top of the hob, and under the glass is a flat copper coil. The alternating current of the coil produces a changing magnetic field whose green field lines loop around the wires of the coil; the outermost ones pass through the glass into the base of the pan. In the base of the pan an eddy current circulates in the opposite direction to the current of the coil. The direction of the current of the coil is marked on the copper-coloured wires with white dots and crosses, and the direction of the eddy current with purple marks. Orange arrows show that energy is transferred from the heating base to the water. No current flows in the glass top.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: valokuidun läpi k: Graph to scale: the power of light passing through an optical fibre as a percentage of the transmitted power, as a function of the length of the fibre over 0–25 kilometres. The solid curve is for a wavelength of 1550 nm with an attenuation of 0.18 dB/km: over 25 kilometres the power falls to 35 per cent. The dashed curve is for a wavelength of 1310 nm with an attenuation of 0.32 dB/km: the power falls to 16 per cent. Dashed lines mark that the power of 1550 nanometre light halves over a distance of 16.7 kilometres.
Periaatekuva langattomasta laturista siv: Schematic of a wireless charger in cross-section, field shape calculated: two panels. In each, at the bottom is the charging pad with the transmitter coil inside it, and above it is the phone, with a receiver coil of the same size in its base. The alternating current of the transmitter coil produces a magnetic field whose green field lines loop around the wires of the coil and pass upward through the middle of the coil. The field lines are drawn at equal flux steps, so the number of lines is proportional to the flux. On the left the phone is 3 millimetres from the charger and on the right 8 millimetres. The lines passing through the receiver coil are drawn darker.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: valokuidun läpi k: Graph to scale: the power of light passing through an optical fibre as a percentage of the transmitted power, as a function of the length of the fibre over 0–40 kilometres. The curve falls from 100 per cent, first steeply and then more gently. The vertical grid lines are five kilometres apart and the horizontal ones ten percentage points apart. No points are marked on the graph.
